chunks: The Shaykh, the jurist, Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Ali ibn al-Husayn ibn Musa ibn Babawayh al-Qummi (may God have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: My father (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Ali ibn Musa ibn Ja'far ibn Abu Ja'far al-Kamandani narrated to us. He said: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa narrated to us, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abu Najran, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad al-Kufi, from Ubaydullah al-Simeen, from Sa'd ibn Turayf, from al-Asbagh ibn Nubata, who said:

While the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) was addressing the people, saying: "Ask me before you lose me, for by God, there is nothing from the past nor anything of the future that you ask me about except that I shall inform you of it." Then Sa'd ibn Abu Waqqas stood up before him and said: "O Commander of the Faithful, tell me how many hairs are on my head and in my beard." He said to him: "Verily, by God, you have asked me about a matter regarding which my friend, the Messenger of God (may God bless him and his family) had told me that you would ask. There is not a single hair on your head or in your beard except that at its root sits a devil. And indeed in your house there is an infant who shall kill al-Husayn, my son." And Umar ibn Sa'd was at that time a toddler, crawling on his hands.

key_terms.خليلي: My intimate friend (khalili) - referring to the Prophet Muhammad (SAWW)
key_terms.سخلا: An infant/suckling (sakhlan) - referring to Umar ibn Sa'd who was a toddler at the time
key_terms.سلوني: Ask me (saluni) - Imam Ali's famous challenge demonstrating his encompassing knowledge

ai.seo_question: What did Imam Ali say about Sa'd ibn Abu Waqqas and the killing of Imam Husayn?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Amali of Shaykh al-Saduq records a dramatic scene in which Imam Ali (AS) invites the people to ask him anything, claiming knowledge of past and future events. When Sa'd ibn Abu Waqqas mockingly asks about the number of hairs on his head, the Imam reveals that the Prophet (SAWW) had forewarned him of this very question, then delivers a devastating prophecy: that every hair on Sa'd's head has a devil at its root, and that Sa'd's infant son, Umar ibn Sa'd, would grow up to be the one who kills Imam al-Husayn (AS). This hadith was understood by the early audience as both a demonstration of the Imam's divinely-granted knowledge and a prophetic foretelling of the tragedy of Karbala.
